analysis.title: "An Additional Use Of Cash": Goldman Finally Counts AI's Off-Balance Sheet Trillions, And $685 Billion Comes Due By 2027
key_insights: Goldman credit strategist Amanda Lynam's Global Markets Daily, "Framing Off-Balance-Sheet Liabilities in the AI Ecosystem", puts Goldman's own numbers on the AI off-balance-sheet pile. Goldman says the category is an additional 'use of cash' beyond consensus capex and that debt financing across syndicated and private markets will play a key role in the AI buildout.

Goldman's tally covers five hyperscalers (Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle). Operating and finance leases total $1.7 trillion, and more than 75% relates to leases not yet commenced, so they are not on the balance sheet as liabilities.
Leases already on the balance sheet are roughly $400 billion. Signed but uncommenced leases are about $1.3 trillion, more than three times the booked lease liabilities.
Goldman puts non-lease unconditional purchase commitments (cloud capacity, servers, networking, power, data center construction) at $1.9 trillion, with $685 billion due by year-end 2027.

Excluding commenced leases, Goldman's off-balance-sheet total for the five hyperscalers is roughly $3.2 trillion. The author's tracker, built from the same 10-Qs and 10-Ks, shows $3.3 trillion: $1.31 trillion of uncommenced leases, $1.77 trillion of purchase commitments, and $212 billion of guarantees and backstops that Goldman excludes. Adding Nvidia, Broadcom and SpaceX gives the author's $4.1 trillion.

The author's tracker has risen from $1.8 trillion in June to $3.1 trillion in August to $4.1 trillion at Q3 filings, against about $1.0 trillion of debt and lease liabilities on the balance sheets. It rose $1 trillion in 90 days.
Moody's put aggregate hyperscaler financial commitments at $2.8 trillion on September 22, up eight-fold since 2023.

Only part of the off-balance-sheet pile shows up in consensus capex. Operating lease payments and third-party cloud contracts run through the income statement, not capex. Goldman equity strategists' $1.7 trillion capex revenue framework excluded off-balance-sheet leases, finance leases, SPVs and 3P compute. Morgan Stanley adds about $195 billion of lease-funded 'synthetic capex' to 2027.

Meta's Q3 10-Q shows $454.5 billion of non-cancelable commitments, about $45.9 billion due in the rest of 2026 and $121.4 billion in 2027, or $167 billion by end of 2027. Meta then tapped shareholders for up to $95 billion.

The $685 billion of purchase commitments due by end-2027 is about 2.5x the record $271 billion of hyperscaler bonds sold so far this year and about 1.6x the roughly $440 billion of hyperscaler debt Goldman expects in 2027. The author notes the comparison is approximate because of overlap with capex already being funded.

Goldman says near-term monetization of AI investment is the key risk to less debt issuance, while delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments are the key risks to more issuance. Purchase commitments grew by more than half a trillion dollars in one quarter on the author's tracker.

Rating agencies are focusing more on these obligations. S&P warned on October 15 that the margin for error is narrowing in the AI funding ecosystem. In late October S&P lowered outlooks on Broadcom (residual value support liabilities) and Meta (leasing leverage).

S&P moved Meta's AA- outlook to negative on October 30. It said leverage could reach 1.3x in 2028 when the proposed El Paso data center lease commences, and it expects a $71 billion free operating cash flow deficit in 2027.

Goldman says evidence of monetization by 2028 is key to mitigating downward ratings pressure. It notes most of the ecosystem is rated near the top of investment grade, so even multi-notch downgrades are unlikely to cut off market access, and compares the path to Pharma's ratings drift lower more than a decade ago.

Goldman expects private capital to play a larger role in AI financing. Preqin counts $19.2 trillion of global private markets AUM with $4.6 trillion of dry powder ($2.9 trillion PE, $1.6 trillion private credit, real estate and infrastructure). Private markets have done more than $225 billion of data center financings since the start of 2025.

Private data center financing in 2026 through October 28 is running at roughly $100 billion, below roughly $130 billion in 2025, with infrastructure funds doing less. The author links this to record private credit defaults, losses at lenders in Meta's Hyperion SPV, and post-election moratoria that Goldman thinks could freeze 45% of planned data center capacity.

$657 billion of AI-related debt has been issued this year, with 41% from the five hyperscalers. The author's view is that hyperscalers burned $31 billion of cash in Q3 and that the debt-funded path is the more likely outcome.

market_movers.rationale: S&P moved Meta's AA- outlook to negative on October 30 on lease-driven leverage, with a $71 billion 2027 free operating cash flow deficit expected. Meta has $167 billion of commitments due by end of 2027 and tapped shareholders for up to $95 billion.
S&P lowered its outlook on Broadcom, citing residual value support liabilities from recent AI compute contracts.
The author suggests CoreWeave may file for bankruptcy, a sarcastic remark about its founder's comment on 'unlimited' private capital. This is not a Goldman call.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman expects heavy debt issuance across syndicated and private markets. It sees ratings pressure as manageable because most issuers are rated near the top of investment grade, with monetization by 2028 as the key mitigant.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's base case is that monetization shows up by 2028, rating agencies stay patient, and private markets fill the gap the bond market cannot. Most of the ecosystem is rated near the top of investment grade, so multi-notch downgrades are unlikely to cut off market access.
tension_points.bear_case: Purchase commitments keep growing faster than AI revenue, leases commence on schedule, and each off-balance-sheet footnote becomes a bond, loan or share sale. Private data center financing is down to about $100 billion from about $130 billion, and S&P has cut outlooks on Meta and Broadcom.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Goldman says evidence of monetization by 2028 is key to mitigating downward pressure on ratings. Delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments are its stated risks to more debt issuance.

theme_stances.key_argument: Off-balance-sheet obligations are an additional use of cash beyond consensus capex, so debt financing across syndicated and private markets will play a key role in the AI buildout.
